title: A design method for pharmacological control of proteins that lack a usable binding pocket

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a broadly generalizable way to start with a chosen protein’s sequence or structure and design a molecule that changes its function, even when that protein has no usable pocket for conventional small-molecule inhibition and no pre-existing target ligand. The intended advance is prospective design: choosing the target first and reliably producing a functional modulator, rather than depending on an already available binder or an exceptional discovery.

A binding pocket is one route to controlling a protein, but it is not the only route. Induced-proximity approaches bring a target together with another cellular component, such as machinery that removes proteins. Conventional small-molecule PROTACs require a target-binding molecule; molecular glues instead promote a productive interaction between proteins. Peptide, nanobody and nucleic-acid approaches already extend access to some proteins without traditional pockets. The proposed advance would provide a general design capability beyond these individual routes and successes.

Scope clarification: the concept’s wording does not restrict the designed molecule to a small molecule. A convincing assessment must therefore specify whether peptides, designed protein binders, nanobodies and oligonucleotides are allowed. That choice changes the challenge and the relevant existing achievements, but does not change the central objective: predictable functional control of a chosen pocketless protein without requiring a pre-existing target ligand.

significance.text: Conventional small-molecule inhibition commonly depends on a suitable catalytic or hydrophobic pocket. A reliable prospective method for controlling proteins without such pockets would substantially expand the accessible drug-target space, potentially including scaffolding proteins, transcription factors and disordered proteins. Its revolutionary importance would lie in making previously difficult targets available for deliberate pharmacological intervention.

Conditional implication: the direct consequences would depend on the effector mechanisms actually demonstrated. A method that reliably induces degradation would establish control over removal of the tested proteins. Demonstrating stabilization or activation as well would broaden that capability, but would not establish freely selectable control over localization, abundance and arbitrary activity. Each additional form of control would require its own evidence.

Conditional downstream possibilities include testing disease mechanisms that are difficult to probe with existing drugs and developing medicines against targets previously inaccessible to conventional inhibitors. These possibilities would still depend on tissue delivery, selectivity, tolerability, resistance and disease-specific clinical benefit. Target engagement alone would not establish therapeutic efficacy, and one approved degrader would not demonstrate the general design method envisioned here.

Disease-activated prodrugs address a different dimension of control: where or when a medicine becomes active. Pocketless-target design addresses which protein can be engaged and functionally controlled. These capabilities can be combined; the supplied PROTAC review describes conditionally activated degraders intended to gate degradation in space or time.

missing_breakthrough.text: The capability sought is repeatable prospective design across diverse chosen pocketless proteins, without needing a known target ligand. The supplied review documents a ligandability bottleneck for conventional small-molecule PROTACs and challenges in predicting productive ternary complexes. It supports the importance of this design problem, but does not establish that every possible general sequence- or structure-based solution is absent as of November 1, 2026.

For induced-proximity implementations, the challenge extends beyond identifying something that binds the target. A designed molecule must support a productive interaction among the target, the molecule and the recruited effector. Rules for designing new protein interfaces are therefore relevant, together with prediction of ternary-complex formation and functional output. The evidence does not establish neo-interface design as the single exclusive barrier, nor justify treating all induced-proximity drugs as dependent on either an existing target ligand or chance discovery.

Engineering synthesis: a practical method must connect molecular design to selective action in human cells. It must distinguish target binding from the intended functional effect, account for access to the relevant cellular compartment, and show that the chosen effector can act on the target in that context. If the goal includes several effector classes, success with degradation cannot substitute for demonstrating stabilization or activation. The relative difficulty of these barriers will depend on the permitted molecular modality and target class.

Benchmarking synthesis: 'no usable pocket' needs an operational definition. A protein that lacks a known inhibitor is not automatically a protein without any usable binding site. Target selection must document the basis for inclusion and distinguish absence of a conventional occupancy-control pocket from absence of all possible molecular recognition. Otherwise, a benchmark could overstate progress by relabeling targets that were already accessible through another route.

current_state.text: The review by Wu and colleagues, published May 20, 2026, describes PROTACs as an established clinical-development modality, including orally bioavailable candidates and late-stage oncology programs. Conventional PROTAC architecture is modular when a suitable target ligand exists. These are review-level reports of clinical development; the supplied material does not provide independently inspected trial results establishing clinical efficacy or the proposed general pocketless-target design capability.

The review contains a staging inconsistency relevant to interpreting its clinical summary: its introduction groups KT-474 with late-stage candidates, while section 3.2 and Table 2 identify it as Phase II. The broader statement about late-stage development is supported by separate oncology programs. KT-474 should therefore not be used here as the example establishing that claim.

Molecular glues can provide access to some targets that conventional inhibitors cannot readily address. The May 2026 review characterizes their discovery as traditionally serendipitous and their target scope as restricted; this does not mean that every glue is discovered by chance. The review also identifies disordered scaffolding proteins as comparatively underexplored. These observations describe limitations and uneven coverage, rather than proving that all pocketless proteins remain inaccessible.

Existing alternatives complicate a simple division between known-ligand PROTACs and chance-discovered glues. The same review describes peptide, nanobody and nucleic-acid approaches for some pocketless targets. In particular, its body text discusses TRAFTACs and aptamer-based PROTACs as routes to transcription factors and RNA-binding proteins lacking traditional hydrophobic pockets. These examples establish relevant routes around conventional pocket dependence, but do not by themselves demonstrate the broad prospective design capability proposed here.

The abstract of The evolving landscape of drug targets, published September 21, 2026, reports 686 biomolecules modulated by 1,702 drugs. Its supplied supplementary information identifies an approval cutoff of June 2025. These figures describe the therapeutic mechanism-of-action targets included in that review. They include nonprotein biomolecules and are neither a count of all ligandable proteins nor a measured fraction of the human proteome. They therefore cannot quantify the share of proteins that this proposed innovation would make accessible.

Access limits matter for interpreting those counts: the supplied evidence review had the Nature article’s subscription abstract preview and a complete five-page supplement, rather than the main review’s full analysis. The abstract supports the headline numbers, and the supplement supports the approval cutoff; unseen main-text methods and figures cannot supply further conclusions. The Frontiers findings above rest on the supplied review’s assessment of article text, without relying on uninspected figure images.

Evidence boundary: the supplied material does not verify the separate estimate that roughly 80 percent of the proteome lacks functional ligands, so that number is not used. No bounded freshness search record was supplied. The May and September 2026 publications support dated statements within their scope, but do not establish comprehensive field status on November 1, 2026. This limitation leaves the breadth of existing prospective design methods unresolved; it is not evidence that an unverified result is false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration, not an established standard: pre-specify a diverse panel of proteins judged to lack usable occupancy-control pockets, document that judgment, and define the permitted molecular modalities. Register the success threshold, screening budget and allowed experimental feedback before testing. Starting from sequence or structure without requiring pre-existing target ligands, the method should produce selective functional modulators in human cells across the panel.
completion_criteria.label: Prospective design yields selective human-cell modulators across prespecified pocketless proteins

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evidence requirements: report every attempted target, the number and nature of candidates tested, functional success rates, unsuccessful designs and any target-specific optimization. Use mechanism controls that distinguish the intended target-dependent effect from nonspecific toxicity or unrelated cellular changes. The denominator and experimental budget are essential to assessing whether the outcome reflects a repeatable design method rather than rare hits from a large search.
completion_criteria.label: Complete target-attempt accounting reports success rates and experimental budgets

completion_criteria.text: Proposed breadth and reproducibility requirements: demonstrate at least two effector classes, such as degradation and stabilization or activation, with suitable evidence for each mechanism. Reproduce results on held-out targets and through independent experimental replication, while reporting the target classes and cellular contexts in which the method fails. A finite panel would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality or automatic access to every effector function.
completion_criteria.label: Two effector classes reproduced on held-out targets with independent replication

completion_criteria.text: Proposed translational milestone: at least one previously unligandable target should show clinical target engagement by a molecule produced through the method, with the prior ligandability assessment and the method’s contribution documented. This would add evidence of human applicability beyond establishing the design principle. It would not by itself demonstrate efficacy, acceptable long-term safety or delivery to every tissue. A single cereblon glue or a PROTAC built on a known inhibitor would not establish the proposed general capability.
completion_criteria.label: Method-designed molecule demonstrates clinical engagement of a previously unligandable target

related_concepts.text: Technical overlap: molecular glues, conventional PROTACs, designed binders, peptide and nucleic-acid degraders, and ternary-interface prediction are relevant enabling approaches. Some already address particular pocketless targets. PHA-01 concerns the breadth and predictability of prospective functional design across chosen targets, so an achievement in any one approach must be assessed against that broader objective.

Roster comparison, synthesized from the supplied titles: PHA-02 concerns predicting human efficacy, dose and major toxicity before exposure; PHA-03 concerns preventing idiosyncratic immune-mediated injury; and PHA-13 concerns a medicine maintaining its own therapeutic window. All could affect whether a pocketless-target modulator becomes useful, but target accessibility does not solve prediction, immune safety or autonomous exposure control.

Roster comparison: PHA-05 addresses systemic access to brain parenchyma for arbitrary drug classes, while PHA-11 addresses reliable oral systemic exposure for folded peptides and proteins. These delivery capabilities could enable PHA-01 molecules, especially if its permitted modalities include peptides or proteins. Designing a functional modulator does not establish either delivery breakthrough.

Roster comparison: PHA-07 concerns dismantling established pathogenic protein conformations and restoring function. It overlaps with PHA-01 when the relevant protein is pocketless or an induced-proximity mechanism is useful. Removing a protein, however, is not equivalent to repairing its pathogenic conformation or restoring its normal function; the two concepts require different functional demonstrations.

Roster comparison: PHA-04 concerns antigen-chosen control of immune memory, PHA-06 concerns in-place replacement of missing human cell types, and PHA-12 concerns triggering scarless regrowth of complex adult mammalian structures. Pocketless-target modulators could become tools within these programs, but access to a molecular target does not establish antigen specificity, cell replacement or coordinated regeneration.

Roster comparison: PHA-08 concerns eradicating dormant infectious persisters without seeding genetic resistance, PHA-09 concerns changing the human aging rate across organ systems, and PHA-10 concerns severe analgesia uncoupled from respiratory depression and reinforcement. PHA-01 might expand the targets available for pursuing these outcomes, but does not establish persister eradication, resistance avoidance, altered aging or separation of analgesia from those adverse effects.

change_log.change: Preserved PHA-01 and its title while defining the advance as broadly generalizable prospective functional design.
change_log.reason: The concept remains meaningful despite uncertainty about the completeness of the supplied account of existing methods.

change_log.change: Replaced the exhaustive ligand-or-chance account of induced proximity with distinctions among conventional PROTACs, molecular glues and alternative molecular modalities.
change_log.reason: The supplied review describes peptide, nanobody and nucleic-acid routes to some pocketless targets.

change_log.change: Qualified claims that the capability is absent and that neo-interface design is its sole barrier.
change_log.reason: The sources document ligandability and ternary-complex challenges without establishing exhaustive field-wide absence.

change_log.change: Restricted direct impact to demonstrated effector functions and retained broader outcomes as conditional possibilities.
change_log.reason: Degradation plus another function would not establish arbitrary activity or localization control.

change_log.change: Preserved clinical-development progress while identifying the review’s KT-474 staging inconsistency.
change_log.reason: Separate oncology programs support late-stage development, but KT-474 is identified as Phase II elsewhere in the same review.

change_log.change: Retained the 686-biomolecule and 1,702-drug counts with the June 2025 approval cutoff and access limitations.
change_log.reason: These are included therapeutic-target counts, not measurements of proteome ligandability; the main Nature analysis was not available in the supplied review.

change_log.change: Excluded the unverified 80-percent estimate and did not repeat the alleged retrieval failure as fact.
change_log.reason: Neither the estimate nor that process history was verified in the supplied material.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria with prospective registration, explicit denominators, screening budgets, mechanism controls and reproducibility.
change_log.reason: These proposed measures make design reliability and demonstrated breadth assessable without implying a consensus threshold or universality.

change_log.change: Separated clinical target engagement from proof of the design principle and from clinical benefit.
change_log.reason: Clinical engagement is an additional proposed translational milestone, not an established requirement for demonstrating molecular design.

change_log.change: Added distinctions covering every other supplied roster entry and retained the prodrug comparison without invoking an unavailable historical list.
change_log.reason: Related capabilities may combine with PHA-01 but have separate outcomes and completion requirements.

unresolved_issues: The permitted molecular modalities remain unspecified, particularly whether the goal is restricted to small molecules or includes peptides, protein binders, nanobodies and oligonucleotides.
Operational definitions of a usable occupancy-control pocket and a previously unligandable target remain to be set.
The target panel, success threshold, screening budget, permitted optimization and replication requirements have not been specified numerically.
The supplied evidence does not establish whether an existing method already meets some or all of the proposed prospective-design objective; no bounded freshness search record was supplied.
The Nature review’s full main analysis was unavailable in the supplied review, limiting assessment of the headline counts’ detailed methodology.
The KT-474 staging inconsistency remains unresolved; the late-stage statement relies on separate oncology programs.
The separate 80-percent chemoproteomic estimate remains unverified and is not used.
The historical breakthrough list referenced in the research was not supplied, so its specific comparisons cannot be assessed.

brief.title: Designing molecules to control hard-to-reach proteins
possible: Researchers could choose a protein involved in disease and design a molecule to change what it does, starting from its sequence or shape. They could do this even when the protein has no suitable binding pocket—a cavity where conventional drugs attach—and no molecule already known to bind it.
why: This would open more proteins to deliberate drug development, including proteins that organize cell machinery or control gene activity. Researchers could test disease mechanisms that existing drugs struggle to probe and pursue treatments against previously inaccessible targets.

sources.who: Nuofan Wu, Zihui Xu, Shuhong Dai and Qianqian Wang
sources.showed: Their review describes molecules that recruit cellular machinery to destroy selected proteins, including candidates in late-stage cancer trials. It also describes approaches that reach some proteins without conventional binding pockets.
sources.cited_for: Existing protein-removal approaches offer routes around conventional pockets, but designing them still faces binding and prediction barriers.
sources.not_established: These approaches do not establish reliable design across diverse chosen proteins without a molecule already known to bind each target.

sources.showed: Their review maps the biological targets through which drugs produce therapeutic effects, identifying 686 biomolecules.
sources.quote: the number and type of targets through which drugs mediate their therapeutic effects, which now include 686 biomolecules
sources.cited_for: The review describes the range of biological targets already reached by medicines.
sources.not_established: Its target count does not measure how many proteins lack usable binding pockets or how many a general design method could reach.

shown: Wu and colleagues describe protein-removing molecules in clinical development and several ways to reach particular proteins without conventional pockets. These include molecular glues, which bring proteins together. Such successes establish routes to individual targets; they do not establish predictable design across diverse chosen proteins.
missing: A repeatable method must turn a chosen protein’s sequence or shape into selective functional control in human cells without an existing binder.
Designed molecules must reach the right cellular location and produce the intended effect, beyond simply attaching to the protein.
Reliable control must extend beyond protein removal to other demonstrated effects, such as stabilization or activation.
A molecule produced by the method must engage a previously inaccessible target in patients.

milestones.label: Designed molecules selectively control a prespecified protein panel
milestones.explanation: A method would have to control diverse proteins in human cells without existing binders, under preset pocket criteria, molecule types, success thresholds and testing limits. This would test deliberate design across chosen targets.

milestones.label: Complete testing accounts establish success rates and effort
milestones.explanation: Every target attempt, candidate, failure and refinement would have to be reported, with controls excluding unrelated effects or toxicity. This would reveal whether success is repeatable at a practical experimental cost.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce distinct forms of control
milestones.explanation: At least two kinds of effect would have to work on targets excluded from development, with independent replication and reported failure contexts. This would establish breadth beyond protein removal within tested boundaries.

milestones.label: A designed molecule reaches its target in patients
milestones.explanation: A molecule made by the method would have to engage a previously inaccessible target in patients, with its design contribution documented. This would establish human applicability without proving treatment benefit or long-term safety.

uncertain: The allowed molecules remain undecided: small molecules alone, or also peptides, proteins and nucleic acids.
A usable binding pocket and a previously inaccessible target need clear definitions; lacking a known inhibitor is insufficient.
The target mix, required success rate, testing budget, allowed refinement and replication standards remain to be set.

page.title: Prospective modulator design for pocketless proteins
page.definition: A sequence- or structure-based method designs molecules that alter the abundance or activity of chosen proteins lacking conventional small-molecule binding pockets, without requiring an existing target ligand. A binding pocket is a cavity accommodating a ligand; eligible modulators include small molecules, peptides, proteins and oligonucleotides.

goal.need: A census covering approvals through June 2025 identifies 1,702 drugs and 686 biomolecular mechanism-of-action targets, including 610 human targets. These counts describe therapeutic mechanisms, not the fraction of proteins with binding pockets. Target 2035 seeks modulators for every human protein; designing modulators without a starting ligand addresses targets outside established ligand collections.

figures.note: Targets follow the review's counting rules, including consolidation of some protein complexes.

statements.body: Structural Genomics Consortium and Target 2035 Working Groups
statements.quote: develop a potent and selective pharmacological modulator for every human protein
statements.context: The roadmap states Target 2035's objective; its computational programme initially concerns small-molecule hit discovery.

statements.quote: rational, target-centric discovery of potent and selective MGDs with favorable drug-like properties
statements.context: The company's Form 10-K describes its discovery objective. MGDs are molecular-glue degraders, small molecules that promote protein interactions leading to degradation.

statements.body: Chatterjee laboratory and collaborators, developers of PepMLM
statements.quote: bind and modulate any target protein, whether structured or not.
statements.context: The discussion describes the intended capability of sequence-designed peptide guides coupled to protein-degradation or stabilization machinery.

completion.title: An independent laboratory designs modulators for new pocketless targets from different protein families.
completion.criterion: An independent laboratory applies a published sequence- or structure-based procedure prospectively to at least two previously untested targets from different protein families. Each target has documented structural or biophysical evidence against a conventional small-molecule pocket; lacking a known inhibitor alone is insufficient. Without a starting target ligand, the procedure yields a molecule for each target that changes its endogenous abundance or activity in human cells, with binding and mechanism controls excluding nonspecific toxicity. The permitted modality and intended effect are fixed before design.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no outside body located defines this combined design-capability test.
completion.basis: Searches of Target 2035 roadmaps, SGC/EUbOPEN probe criteria, DARPA/ARPA-H programmes and molecular-glue/binder benchmarks found no published test for this combined capability. Two families are the minimum interpretation of transfer across protein families; independent prospective use tests transfer of the procedure. Chemical-probe criteria assess individual compounds. The cited cellular demonstrations do not report this validation.

milestones.title: A designed molecule binds a chosen pocketless protein in two orthogonal experimental assays.
milestones.criterion: Confirm physical target engagement, alone or in the intended protein complex, using two assays based on different physical principles. Design must not require a starting target ligand. Published evidence: Sun and colleagues expressed 14 protein designs and advanced 8 soluble designs to functional testing. B9 binding to TDP-43's low-complexity domain was examined by biolayer interferometry and nuclear magnetic resonance; its reported dissociation constant was 87.9 ± 2.7 nM. The paper was published on 3 September 2025.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback extending the two-assay validation in Target 2035's Table 2, which was written for predicted small-molecule hits, to all eligible modalities.

milestones.title: A designed molecule changes a pocketless protein's abundance or activity in human cells.
milestones.criterion: A sequence- or structure-designed molecule changes its target's endogenous abundance or activity in human cells, with controls establishing target dependence and the intended mechanism. Hong and colleagues reported stabilization of endogenous PAX3::FOXO1 in RH4 cells for 5 of 10 sequence-designed peptide–deubiquitinase fusions, with 3 biological replicates. Their paper, published on 15 April 2025, supplies cellular evidence; it does not establish proteome-wide selectivity or a general success rate.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback; no cellular-effect threshold covering every eligible modality was located. EUbOPEN publishes numerical criteria for small-molecule chemical probes.

milestones.title: One method yields cellular modulators for at least two pocketless targets from different protein families.
milestones.criterion: The same published procedure yields functional human-cell modulators for at least two prospectively chosen pocketless targets from different protein families, without a starting target ligand. Pocket suitability and intended effect are specified before design. PepMLM, published online on 13 August 2025, reports degradation of huntingtin-related and viral proteins. Related deubiquibodies demonstrate stabilization. These results bear on transfer across targets but were not a prespecified cross-family pocketless-target test.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback; Target 2035 proposes prediction for targets absent from training data, but supplies no acceptance threshold for functional control across pocketless target families.

milestones.title: A new study replicates cellular modulation by the method's designed molecules.
milestones.criterion: Using newly collected data, a separate study reproduces the cellular effects of the designed molecules used to establish cross-family performance. Effects are consistent within measurement uncertainty for the same targets and intended mechanisms. Reanalysis of original data and replicate wells within the original study do not satisfy this test.
milestones.set_by: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, Reproducibility and Replicability in Science, Conclusion 3-1; its general replication criterion is applied to these cellular results.
milestones.threshold_quote: Replicability is obtaining consistent results across studies aimed at answering the same scientific question, each of which has obtained its own data.

not_found: No published completion benchmark covering prospective functional design across pocketless protein families and all eligible molecular modalities was located.
No modality-independent operational definition of a usable protein binding pocket was located.
No externally set target-panel size, success-rate threshold or experimental design budget was located for this capability.
No separate study replicating the cited cross-family cellular results, or independent prospective validation on new pocketless target families, was located.
The publisher HTML for The evolving landscape of drug targets could not be opened; a full-text manuscript copy was available.
